newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl declines comment on France's EMU chances.
newsitem.headline: Kohl declines comment on France's EMU chances.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl declined on Friday to comment when asked about France's chances of being at the launch of European economic and monetary union (EMU) scheduled to go ahead on January 1, 1999.
"We should leave the French to do what they themselves want to do. It is not for me to say," Kohl told a news conference when asked how he rated the country's chances of joining EMU.
Kohl said German-Franco relations were very close and Bonn's relations with French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin "extremely positive."
"German-Franco ties are close and in a state of normality," Kohl said.

German-Franco ties have been strained since France's new Socialist government suggested it would not meet the three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) entry criterion to qualify for EMU. An independent audit was expected next week to show a deficit above 3.5 percent of GDP this year.
Kohl and Jospin have set a date to clear the air in Franco-German relations in what could be a decisive step towarcd a single European currency.
They are due to meet on August 28 in Bonn to try to overcome strains between the two countries which pride themselves on working together as the motor of European integration.
